title: Perfect constant models for stratified finite-field etale complexes
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $k$ be a finite field. Let $L\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},k)$ be a bounded complex in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of sheaves of modules over the constant sheaf $k_X$ on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose every cohomology sheaf is constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. There is a finite stratification of $X$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-constructible-subset] such that on an etale covering of each stratum $S$, $L|_S$ is isomorphic to the constant sheaf complex of a bounded complex of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces; in particular the constant complex is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. After pro-etale comparison these are also the models of $(\nu_X^*L)|_S$, using [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. No integral lifting or completeness hypothesis is involved.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, forward implication, residue stratification; Proposition 6.8.11(3)

proof.text: Choose $a\leq b$ with $H^q(L)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-stratified-cohomology-slice-models] with $B=k$. It gives a finite constructible locally closed stratification $i_s:S_s\to X$ and $K_s=i_s^{-1}L$, vanishing outside the same interval, whose cohomology has finite constant trivializations on every etale slice.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-bounded-constant-models] to each $K_s$, using precisely those slice trivializations and $a\leq b$. Obtain a jointly surjective etale cover $v_j:U_j\to S_s$ and actual finite $k$-module complexes $P_j^\bullet$, zero outside $[a,b]$, with $v_j^{-1}K_s\cong Q\underline{P_j^\bullet}$. The canonical module inverse-image composition isomorphism identifies the left side with $(i_sv_j)^{-1}L$; termwise exact localization gives the same comparison in the derived category.

The finite set underlying each $P_j^q$ generates it: every element is already one of the generators. Thus its terms are finitely generated, and they are projective by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-projective]. The same zero-term bounds make $P_j^\bullet$ bounded. Consequently $P_j^\bullet$ itself, with the identity derived isomorphism, witnesses perfectness by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex].

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, meaning of perfect values, specialized to a field

proof.text:
For $h=i_sv_j$ use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coefficient-derived-model-comparison]. Apply $N_{U_j}^D$ to the etale model $e:h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1,D}L\cong Q\underline{P_j^\bullet}$ and compose its image with the two comparisons from that node:
$$F_h^DN_X^DL\cong N_{U_j}^Dh_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1,D}L\xrightarrow{N_{U_j}^D(e)}N_{U_j}^DQ\underline{P_j^\bullet}\cong E_{U_j}^DQ\underline{P_j^\bullet}_{\mathrm{proet}}.$$
This supplies the pro-etale model with exactly the same complex and etale cover, completing both assertions.
